name: Psaltery
overview: The Psaltery, as depicted in Scripture, was a significant musical instrument used in worship and religious ceremonies, particularly in Israel’s praise to God. David and the people of Israel played psalteries with other instruments to honor the LORD with singing and music, demonstrating wholehearted devotion (2 Samuel 6:5; 1 Chronicles 13:8). The instrument was integral to organized temple worship, led by appointed musicians such as Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who prophesied and served in the house of the LORD through music (1 Chronicles 16:5; 1 Chronicles 25:1,6). Additionally, psalteries were part of celebrations marking the dedication of the new wall after the captivity, highlighting their role in significant communal and spiritual events, though they were also sometimes associated with idolatrous worship practices.
